title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, Internal Tools (v2)
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Summary

This consolidated handbook page provides the canonical company-level guidance for working at Redwood: role summaries and career ladder expectations, benefits and perks overview, hiring and 90-day onboarding checklist, and a concise internal tools guide and ops flows. Audience: all Redwood employees, managers, and new hires. Team-specific ladders, compensation guidance, and interview rubrics are linked at the end.

1) Company context and working norms

- Mission: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.
- Ways of working: engineering-first, customer-focused, data-informed decisions, with a bias for operational reliability.
- Remote & flexible work: Redwood supports hybrid and remote-first teams. Managers may define core collaboration hours when necessary; exceptions go through People Ops.

2) Roles & career ladder summaries (overview)

Redwood maintains leveled ladders to make expectations explicit for scope, autonomy, and impact. Detailed competency matrices and example deliverables are maintained by People Ops and managers. The brief ladder below is a summary for common tracks.

Engineering (IC track):
- E1 / New Grad: learns codebase, ships small tasks with mentorship, follows testing and review conventions.
- E2 / Software Engineer: independently owns features of moderate scope, writes tests, participates in design discussions.
- E3 / Senior Software Engineer: leads large features, mentors peers, owns service reliability and operational runbooks.
- E4 / Staff Engineer: drives architecture for multiple services, removes cross-team barriers, sets technical direction in an area.
- E5 / Principal / Distinguished Engineer: shapes company-wide technical strategy, leads mission-critical initiatives and incubates new platform capabilities.

Product & Design:
- PM1–PM3 and Designer I–III: progression from feature ownership to product area strategy, cross-functional leadership, and measurable business outcomes.

Customer Success, Sales & GTM:
- IC to manager tracks: starts with onboarding / adoption-focused roles and progresses to strategic account and team leadership roles.

People Ops, Security, Finance, Legal:
- Professional laddering parallels engineering but adapts to function-specific competencies (policy, compliance, audit readiness, vendor management).

Promotion flow (summary):
1. Initiation: candidate or manager prepares a promotion packet (examples of work, impact statement, manager feedback).
2. Calibration: cross-functional review panel evaluates against ladder criteria.
3. Decision & feedback: People Ops communicates outcome and next steps.
4. Timing: standing promotion cycles are quarterly; exceptional promotions may be approved outside the cycle.

3) Benefits and perks (high level)

- Health & wellness: multiple medical, dental, and vision plans; Redwood subsidizes a significant portion of premiums. Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and mental health sessions available.
- Financial: 401(k) with company match, equity awards with standard 4-year vesting and 1-year cliff, salary reviews on promotion and annually.
- Time off: flexible PTO, paid parental leave (gender neutral), company holidays and optional office closures. Minimum guidance: 15 days PTO baseline.
- Workplace support: home office stipend, ergonomic equipment requests, commuter benefits where applicable.
- Learning & development: $1,500 learning stipend per year plus conference allowance; internal training programs and mentorship.

Notes: benefits eligibility generally begins the first of the month following 30 days of employment for full-time employees. Contractors and contingent workers have separate policies. Use the Benefits Portal to enroll and the Finance expense system for reimbursements.

4) Hiring and onboarding (end-to-end overview)

Hiring: core steps
1. Requisition: hiring manager opens a requisition in Greenhouse with role profile, compensation band, and hiring timeline. People Ops confirms headcount and budget.
2. Interview loop: hiring manager designs the loop with recruiting and selects appropriate rubrics. Standardized scorecards are required for bias mitigation.
3. Candidate evaluation: interviews use calibrated scorecards; senior hires require calibration committee review.
4. Offer & acceptance: People Ops drafts the offer and coordinates approvals.

Onboarding (first 90 days): checklist
- Before Day 1: equipment order, Okta provisioning, GitHub and Slack invites, welcome note and orientation schedule.
- Day 1: company orientation, security baseline training, benefits enrollment guidance, team intro, and buddy assignment.
- Week 1: set up dev environment, access to necessary repos, first 1:1 with manager, define 30/60/90 goals.
- Weeks 2–4: role-specific ramp tasks, join team rituals, initial project assignment and mentor pairing.
- Month 1–3: measurable deliverables, public demo of first contribution, 30-day and 90-day check-ins; formal 90-day onboarding review with manager.

New-hire buddy program
- A buddy from the hiring team is assigned on Day 1 to help with practical questions, tooling, and cultural context. Buddy responsibilities include weekly check-ins during month one and helping escalate access issues.

Access & security for new hires
- Default access sequence: Okta -> Slack -> Confluence -> GitHub -> Cloud console (GCP/AWS) -> Datadog/Honeycomb (read).
- Elevated privileges (production write, KMS, service account creation) require manager justification, Security team approval, and a documented two-person authorization where applicable.
- Offboarding must revoke all accounts within 24 hours of separation; managers coordinate asset return and knowledge handover with People Ops.

5) Internal tools quick guide & common flows

Primary systems and intended usage
- Slack: synchronous and asynchronous team communication. Use public channels for discoverability; keep PII out of public channels. Threads for topic continuity.
- Confluence: canonical documentation, runbooks, and onboarding material. Each team maintains a landing page and a page index.
- GitHub: source control, PRs, and CI. Follow branch naming conventions and required reviews.
- Jira / Linear: issue tracking, sprint planning, and prioritization. Label cross-team work clearly.
- Okta: identity and SSO provider. Report broken provisioning via IT ticket.
- Cloud consoles (GCP/AWS): production and staging access controlled via IAM groups. Requests for privilege changes go through the infra-oncall ticket workflow.
- Datadog / Honeycomb: observability and tracing. Tagging standard: service:, env:, team:.
- PagerDuty: incident notification and on-call rotations. Maintain accurate escalation paths.

Common requests & procedures
- Create a new repository: open an infra-tooling ticket with repo name, owner, CI requirements, and CODEOWNERS.
- Request cloud or elevated access: submit the Access Request form in the IT portal with manager approval and an intended expiration date.
- Report a security incident: immediately page Security on-call via PagerDuty and open a security-incident ticket in Jira. Avoid sharing sensitive details in public Slack channels until Security advises.

Naming conventions (summary)
- Confluence page titles: kebab-case for URLs; include a concise descriptive title.
- Git branches: feature/<ticket>-short-desc or fix/<ticket>-short-desc.
- Service names: <team>-<service>-<env>. Example: infra-router-prod.

6) Manager responsibilities & People Ops partnership

- Managers: career development, feedback cadence, performance calibration, team hiring, and workload balance. Managers are responsible for ensuring direct reports have clear 30/60/90 plans and receive timely feedback.
- People Ops: policy governance, promotion calibration support, benefits administration, interview training, and diversity & inclusion programs.

7) Offboarding, role transitions & knowledge transfer

- Offboarding steps: resignation notice -> manager notification -> People Ops coordinates IT and Security actions -> knowledge transfer and runbook updates -> equipment return and final payroll processing.
- Knowledge transfer checklist: update runbooks, reassign open PRs and tickets, document active on-call responsibilities, and schedule stakeholder handoffs.

8) Quick contacts & links
